svg.text: Figure 6. Clinical context on the NLST test split (exploratory): the same false-alarm levels, and cuts set on development data
false alarms per 1,000 exams (axis broken between 175 and 310)
L4, cancers caught of 86: Sybil 61, Form 73, Brock 64, Lung-RADS >= 4A 67
L3, cancers caught of 86: Sybil 69, Form 77, Brock 70, Lung-RADS >= 3 68
R, cancers caught of 86: Sybil 82, Form 83, Brock 79, call 81
false alarms per 1,000 exams (axis broken between 175 and 310)
L4, cancers caught of 131: Sybil 54, Form 52, Brock 53, Lung-RADS >= 4A 48
L3, cancers caught of 131: Sybil 63, Form 59, Brock 59, Lung-RADS >= 3 54
R, cancers caught of 131: Sybil 86, Form 100, Brock 76, call 78
Form (radiologists' findings + age, sex, smoking; fitted on NLST train)
Brock (published; no family history in the public data)
Levels: cuts set on cancer-free DEV exams to the dev false-alarm share of Lung-RADS >= 4A (L4), >= 3 (L3) and the radiologists' call (R). Lines: 95% participant-bootstrap intervals.
Sybil's score has steps: at R its dev false-alarm share was 36.0% (target 34.3%) at 1 year and 36.5% (target 38.3%) at 6 years, part of its lower false alarms there.
1 year: the form and the fixed rules use the radiologists' reads, which also triggered the work-up (not blind to the outcome). 6 years at baseline avoids the prior-scan advantage and
reduces 1-year work-up bias, but Lung-RADS and Brock score nodules only: 55 of the 131 six-year cancers (7 of 86 one-year) had no nodule >= 4 mm on the scan.
Lung-RADS and Brock were reconstructed from the NLST forms (part-solid size assumed; Brock without family history).
1 year, baseline screens only (41 cancers): at L3 Sybil 36, form 37, Lung-RADS >= 3 32; at R Sybil 39 (356 false alarms per 1,000), form 39 (408), call 39 (406).
Threshold transfer, 1 year, all screens: development (hollow) -> test (filled)
false alarms per 1,000, dev -> test; cancers caught on test
cut set on cancer-free dev exams (L3): false alarms transfer; dev sensitivity was inflated for Sybil
cut matched on dev CANCERS (to the radiologists' dev sensitivity): false alarms not matched; Sybil's sensitivity collapses
Dev results flatter Sybil: Sybil's developers selected the model on this split, so its dev sensitivity is optimistic and a cut tuned to dev cancers sits too high on new data.
